title: Switched gates yield bounded-width clean DNFs
statement: Let $n$, $m$, and $l$ be natural numbers, let $\rho_1$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, and let $g_1, \dots, g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ variables. For each $i$, write $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ for the restricted Boolean function $x \mapsto g_i\bigl(\rho_1.\mathrm{extend}\,x\bigr)$, that is, $g_i$ evaluated on the input obtained by setting the fixed coordinates of $\rho_1$ and reading the free coordinates from $x$. Suppose that for every $i$ the decision-tree depth of $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ is at most $l$. Then there exist DNF formulas $g_1', \dots, g_m'$ such that, for every $i$: the width of $g_i'$ is at most $l$; $g_i'$ computes $g_i|_{\rho_1}$ on every input; within each term of $g_i'$ any two literals on the same variable are identical; and no term of $g_i'$ contains a repeated literal.
hypotheses_covered: a family of m DNF formulas g_i on n variables
a restriction ρ₁ on n variables
for each gate i, the decision-tree depth of the restricted function g_i|_{ρ₁} is at most l
replaced:
Suppose for each gate $i$ the restricted function $\mathrm{restrictFn}\,(\mathrm{gates}\,i).\mathrm{eval}\,\rho_1$
has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then there exist DNFs $\mathrm{gates}'$ such that each
$(\mathrm{gates}'\,i)$ has width at most $l$, evaluates to the corresponding restricted gate
function on every input, and is clean: within each term every literal is determined by its
variable (injectivity on variables) and each term has no duplicate literals.
